record.paper_title: Mini-Proceedings ECT* Workshop: Hadronic Atoms and Kaonic Nuclei
record.original_question: Was the historical kaonic helium puzzle—the five-sigma discrepancy between theoretical expectations of an approximately zero eV strong-interaction shift for the kaonic helium-4 2p state and older measurements averaging about −43 eV—resolved by newer E570 and SIDDHARTA measurements showing a shift consistent with 0 eV?

evidence.quote: Prior to the experiment by the E570 group, the average of the three previous results was −43 ± 8 eV [3], while most of the theoretical calculations give ∼0 eV [2]. This five-sigma discrepancy between theory and experiment was known as the ‘kaonic helium puzzle.’ A resolution of this long-standing puzzle provided by the E570 group is now firmly established by the present work.
A new value of the strong interaction shift of the kaonic helium-4 2p state was determined to be 0 ± 6 (stat) ± 2 (syst) eV [1].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A kaonic helium atom is formed when a negatively charged kaon (K^-) is captured by a helium nucleus and cascades down through atomic orbitals, replacing an electron. For the 2p state of kaonic helium-4 (K^- ^4He), the strong K^-–nucleus interaction produces a small shift ΔE_{2p} of the level energy relative to the purely electromagnetic value predicted by QED. Theoretical optical-potential calculations predict |ΔE_{2p}| of order 0 eV (at most a few eV), whereas three early X-ray spectroscopy experiments performed in the 1970s–1980s yielded a weighted average ΔE_{2p} ≈ −43 ± 8 eV, in roughly five-standard-deviation tension with theory. This discrepancy became known as the "kaonic helium puzzle."

Question: Did subsequent precision X-ray measurements of the kaonic helium-4 2p strong-interaction shift (in particular by the E570 experiment at KEK and the SIDDHARTA experiment at DAΦNE) yield a value of ΔE_{2p} statistically consistent with 0 eV, thereby resolving the five-sigma discrepancy with the theoretical prediction?
artifact.status_search_result: Multiple published precision measurements (E570 at KEK, 2007; SIDDHARTA at LNF, 2009) reported the kaonic ^4He 2p strong-interaction shift to be consistent with zero (E570: +2 ± 2(stat) ± 2(syst) eV; SIDDHARTA: 5 ± 3(stat) ± 4(syst) eV), in agreement with theoretical expectations of ~0 eV. The kaonic helium puzzle is widely regarded in the literature as resolved.

status_evidence.title: Measurement of the strong-interaction shift in kaonic-helium-4 atoms (E570)
status_evidence.snippet: We measured the strong-interaction shift of the kaonic-4He 3d→2p X-ray transition... shift of +2 ± 2 (stat) ± 2 (syst) eV, consistent with zero.
status_evidence.claim: E570 measurement gives a shift consistent with 0 eV, resolving the older anomalous −43 eV result.

status_evidence.title: Kaonic helium-4 X-ray measurement by SIDDHARTA
status_evidence.snippet: The strong-interaction shift of the 2p state of kaonic helium-4 was determined to be 5 ± 3 (stat) ± 4 (syst) eV, consistent with zero and with the E570 result.
status_evidence.claim: SIDDHARTA confirms a near-zero 2p shift, in agreement with theory and with E570.
